headline: ‘Mamma Mia’ takes over King Opera House
Denis Villeneuve Wants to Bring James Bond’s Unapologetic Masculinity Back, Says The Character “Deeply Inspires Me”
snippet: Denis Villeneuve is getting his shot at James Bond, and the director sounds like a kid who just got handed the keys to the coolest car on the planet. For the filmmaker, taking on 007 isn't just about making another massive Hollywood blockbuster. He's fascinated by the character's attitude, charisma, and complicated relationship with masculinity. During a recent interview with GQ's Zach Baron in Los Angeles, the Dune director opened up about his love for James Bond, particularly the original version played by Sean Connery. Villeneuve explained: “I adore James Bond. I adore Sean Connery, the Sean Connery years, the birth of James Bond, his panache, his drive, his charisma, his unapologetic way of living, the strength, and what it says, good and bad, about masculinity.” That's an interesting perspective from a director who has spent much of his career exploring complicated characters. Bond has always represented a particular kind of masculinity, one built around confidence, danger, sex appeal, and a complete disregard for anyone telling him what to do. Of course, some of those qualities haven't aged particularly well, and Villeneuve seems interested in examining both sides of what makes 007 such an enduring character. The director also recalled his reaction when the opportunity to direct the next James Bond movie came his way, and he didn't exactly play it cool. “There’s something about James Bond that deeply inspires me. And when I got a call to ask me, if I would be interested, that they will offer me to do James Bond, I just hang up and scream in the street. I mean, of course, I want to do James Bond. And the thing is that it’s a blessing.” It's pretty awesome to hear a filmmaker of Villeneuve's caliber get this excited about a franchise. This isn't some director treating Bond like another studio assignment. He's a genuine fan who clearly has strong feelings about what makes the character work. His upcoming James Bond film will also mark a major turning point for the franchise as the first 007 adventure produced under Amazon MGM Studios' creative control. Robert Pattinson has been confirmed as the new James Bond, and Villeneuve previously celebrated the casting in a statement released by Amazon MGM Studios: “Before anything else, I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey. We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007. I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin.” Pattinson taking over the role is an exciting choice, especially with Villeneuve directing. Both have a knack for bringing something unexpected to familiar material, and their collaboration could give Bond a fresh identity without losing the swagger that made him a cinematic icon. The new James Bond movie is being produced by Amy Pascal and David Heyman, with Tanya Lapointe serving as executive producer. Steven Knight, the creator of Peaky Blinders, is writing the screenplay. Filming is expected to begin in 2027, with a theatrical release reportedly planned for 2028, although an official release date hasn't been announced. Plot details are still being kept under wraps. What makes this project particularly interesting is Villeneuve's appreciation for the contradictions that define James Bond. He clearly loves Connery's take on the character, but he also recognizes that Bond's old-school masculinity comes with some baggage. That could make for a fascinating new direction for 007. The character doesn't need to lose his edge or become a completely different person to work for modern audiences. Villeneuve is the filmmaker who seems to understand why people love this character, and I’m looking forward to seeing what he does with him.

If the documentation explicitly prohibits the use of vinegar or citric acid, specialized descaling agents formulated for that specific brand are the only safe alternative to avoid compromising the integrity of the surface. headline: Truth Commission to hold first national conference
snippet: THE truth commission investigating former president Rodrigo Duterte’s war on drugs will hold its first national conference, six months after its creation in May. During the conference, to be held on Nov. 23, it will present its “Six-Month Report” on its truth-seeking, documentation, survivor accompaniment and accountability work. “The conference will also observe Araw ng Katotohanan (Day of Truth) — a national space to honor victims and survivors, amplify their voices, examine the lessons emerging from the Commission’s work, and strengthen the collective pursuit of truth, justice, healing, and institutional reform,” the commission said on its website. “The Truth Commission will present a series of reports examining the human cost of extrajudicial killings, forensic evidence, trauma and healing, and emerging legal and policy lessons,” it added. The commission announced this on its Facebook page on Tuesday, with Truth Commission Chairman Raul Pangalangan and forensic pathologist and Commissioner Dr. Raquel Fortun discussing the work they have done over the past six months. The conference will be held on Nov. 23 at the Philippine Normal University at 8 a.m. Also, the commission announced that it will hold its 8th truth-telling session on Friday at the Co Po Ty Auditorium at Adamson University. For this session, the commission will talk about barangay (village) public safety officer Angelito Luciano, who was shot dead on the night of Nov. 30, 2016, on Visayas Street in Payatas B, Quezon City. His live-in partner, Reggina Villegas, will speak about Luciano’s life as a father of two children and his work as a public safety officer. “She will also describe finding his body at the scene and the questions the family has never had answered. The effects of the killing on her and their children will also be part of her testimony,” the commission said. The public servant was shot by an unidentified gunman. “Luciano was sitting on his motorcycle when a gunman came up behind him, called him by his nickname and shot him repeatedly, according to accounts Villegas received at the scene. The gunman took Luciano’s own gun before leaving. No suspect has been publicly identified in the 10 years since,” the commission described the death of Luciano. “Luciano’s case reflects a pattern seen in many killings of the period: a man shot on a public street, with no suspect and no explanation for his family. By hearing Villegas, the Commission seeks to restore his name and identify the gaps that have kept such cases unresolved,” it added.

headline: to hold first national conference
snippet: THE truth commission investigating former president Rodrigo Duterte’s war on drugs will hold its first national conference, six months after its creation in May. During the conference, to be held on Nov. 23, it will present its “Six-Month Report” on its truth-seeking, documentation, survivor accompaniment and accountability work. “The conference will also observe Araw ng Katotohanan (Day of Truth) — a national space to honor victims and survivors, amplify their voices, examine the lessons emerging from the Commission’s work, and strengthen the collective pursuit of truth, justice, healing, and institutional reform,” the commission said on its website. “The Truth Commission will present a series of reports examining the human cost of extrajudicial killings, forensic evidence, trauma and healing, and emerging legal and policy lessons,” it added. The commission announced this on its Facebook page on Tuesday, with Truth Commission Chairman Raul Pangalangan and forensic pathologist and Commissioner Dr. Raquel Fortun discussing the work they have done over the past six months. The conference will be held on Nov. 23 at the Philippine Normal University at 8 a.m. Also, the commission announced that it will hold its 8th truth-telling session on Friday at the Co Po Ty Auditorium at Adamson University. For this session, the commission will talk about barangay (village) public safety officer Angelito Luciano, who was shot dead on the night of Nov. 30, 2016, on Visayas Street in Payatas B, Quezon City. His live-in partner, Reggina Villegas, will speak about Luciano’s life as a father of two children and his work as a public safety officer. “She will also describe finding his body at the scene and the questions the family has never had answered. The effects of the killing on her and their children will also be part of her testimony,” the commission said. The public servant was shot by an unidentified gunman. “Luciano was sitting on his motorcycle when a gunman came up behind him, called him by his nickname and shot him repeatedly, according to accounts Villegas received at the scene. The gunman took Luciano’s own gun before leaving. No suspect has been publicly identified in the 10 years since,” the commission described the death of Luciano. “Luciano’s case reflects a pattern seen in many killings of the period: a man shot on a public street, with no suspect and no explanation for his family. By hearing Villegas, the Commission seeks to restore his name and identify the gaps that have kept such cases unresolved,” it added.

headline: DMW, ITF, Amosup sign pact protecting Filipino seafarers
snippet: DRIVEN by the urgent need to protect the world’s largest maritime workforce from escalating geopolitical0 crises, vessel abandonment, and unfair criminalization abroad, the Philippine government and leading maritime unions have forged a unified rapid-response alliance. On Nov. 11, 2026, at the newly renovated Amosup Convention Hall in Intramuros, Manila, Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac, Associated Marine Officers’ and Seamen’s Union of the Philippines (Amosup) president Dr. Conrado Oca, and International Transport Workers’ Federation (ITF) General Secretary Stephen Cotton signed a tripartite memorandum of understanding (MOU) to institutionalize coordinated protection for overseas Filipino seafarers and their families. The signing coincided with the convention hall’s inauguration and Amosup’s 66th founding anniversary, underscoring decades of union advocacy now backed by state machinery. Speaking at the event, Dr. Oca noted that the partnership builds on the legacy of Amosup’s late founder, Capt. Gregorio Oca, and marks the 20th anniversary of the Maritime Labour Convention (MLC), 2006 — the Seafarers’ Bill of Rights — which his father championed. “The signing of the memorandum of understanding between Amosup, the Department of Migrant Workers, and the International Transport Workers’ Federation further solidifies our commitment and reaffirms our shared ideals of protecting and advancing the welfare and best interests of Filipino seafarers around the world,” Dr. Oca said, assuring mariners that as long as Amosup stands, they will never face hardships alone and can sail with peace of mind knowing their families are cared for. Secretary Cacdac hailed the social dialogue between government and labor leaders for cutting through bureaucratic red tape to deliver swift action, noting that the pact fulfills President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s directive to include seafarers’ families in state protection. “This is so timely with the information sharing, case handling, and welfare assistance, particularly in cases involving unpaid wages, employment-related violations, abuse, injury, illness, death, piracy, abandonment, and other maritime emergencies — very timely interventions that we could make,” Cacdac said, adding that as far as the DMW and the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration are concerned, “we are all in this together — all hands on deck.” Echoing this spirit of solidarity, ITF General Secretary Stephen Cotton underscored the power of global unions standing shoulderto-shoulder with Philippine authorities and maritime stakeholders to defend seafarers’ fundamental rights across international waters. Cotton emphasized that as Filipino mariners keep global supply chains moving through volatile seas, cross-border solidarity is vital to hold rogue shipowners accountable, combat abandonment, and stop the unfair criminalization of crews — pledging to mobilize ITF’s global network of port inspectors and affiliated unions to engage flag and port state authorities and insurers whenever Filipino seafarers face distress. At its core, the two-year pact links DMW’s diplomatic mandate with Amosup’s domestic welfare infrastructure and ITF’s global inspectorate, covering Filipino crew members worldwide alongside concerns involving Philippine-flagged vessels or ships in Philippine waters. It directly targets severe maritime crises — establishing real-time risk advisory sharing, coordinated evacuation, and family communication lifelines amid piracy, hostage-taking, and armed conflict, while streamlining legal aid for contract and collective bargaining agreement (CBA) breaches. The pact also confronts vessel abandonment and unpaid wages, where rogue shipowners leave crews stranded in foreign ports without food, fuel, medical care, or pay. Aligned with the MLC 2006, it enables urgent welfare aid and repatriation referrals without waiting out the standard two-month nonpayment threshold when immediate survival needs exist, while committing the parties to draft a national standard operating procedure (SOP) defining stakeholder liabilities. Additionally, it addresses the arbitrary detention and criminalization of mariners abroad by mandating immediate collaboration to secure legal counsel and interpreters, uphold the presumption of innocence, and pursue swift repatriation. Central to the framework is government-led coordination paired with union muscle. The DMW acts as the state anchor — mobilizing Migrant Workers Offices (MWOs), Philippine embassies, and government agencies to act on referrals and coordinate with foreign authorities, while Amosup provides union representation, healthcare via its Seamen’s Hospitals, training through the Maritime Academy of Asia and the Pacific (MAAP), psychosocial care, and regional support via the upcoming Cagayan de Oro Welfare Complex. To ensure rapid execution, the parties will appoint focal persons within 30 days and establish a referral protocol within 60 days, enforcing a zero-delay rule so incomplete paperwork never stalls urgent aid, while upholding data privacy under Republic Act 10173 and guaranteeing that union membership is never required for government assistance.

headline: Rockwell Automation Integrates NVIDIA Omniverse into Emulate3D to Advance Industrial Simulation and AI-Powered Factory Design
snippet: Manufacturers can simulate larger, more complex systems and accelerate AI-driven innovation before physical deployment MILWAUKEE, Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Rockwell Automation, Inc. (NYSE: ROK), the world's largest company dedicated to industrial automation and digital transformation, today announced the integration of NVIDIA Omniverse, NVIDIA RTX and OpenUSD technologies into Emulate3D, expanding the scale, performance and intelligence of industrial simulation for manufacturers. The integration combines Emulate3D's simulation and controls-testing capabilities with NVIDIA Omniverse, NVIDIA RTX rendering and OpenUSD to support factory-scale visualization and virtual commissioning. Manufacturers can model, test and optimize production environments earlier in the design process, helping identify issues and reduce commissioning risk before equipment is deployed. "To accelerate AI adoption across engineering and operations, manufacturers are looking beyond traditional simulation," said Matheus Bulho, senior vice president, Software & Control, Rockwell Automation. "By combining Emulate3D with NVIDIA Omniverse, NVIDIA RTX rendering and OpenUSD, we're enabling customers to simulate larger, more complex systems while providing the foundation for AI systems to learn, validate decisions and optimize performance before deployment. This represents an important step toward a future where AI and human expertise work together to design, build and operate more productive factories." For manufacturers, the value of more advanced simulation is the ability to make critical engineering decisions with greater confidence before they reach the physical environment. "The ability to explore, test and validate ideas virtually is becoming increasingly valuable as manufacturing systems grow in complexity," said Lora Green, senior manager for Advanced Manufacturing Simulation at GE Appliances. "Continued advances in industrial simulation allow us the flexibility to evaluate new ideas earlier, make more informed engineering decisions, and approach deployment with greater confidence." With these expanded capabilities, Emulate3D helps manufacturers move from individual machine and system simulation toward more complex, factory-scale environments. This creates a stronger digital foundation for testing designs, operational strategies and AI-enabled workflows before physical commissioning. Key benefits: Simulate larger and more complex manufacturing systems, including full-scale factory environments. Accelerate physically accurate simulation and visualization fidelity with NVIDIA Omniverse, RTX and OpenUSD technologies Create virtual environments for testing, validation and optimization before physical deployment. Provide deterministic outcomes that help improve AI-driven engineering and operational decisions. Reduce commissioning risk by identifying issues earlier in the design process. Support the development of AI-enabled workflows across engineering and factory operations. Additional information about Emulate3D can be found at www.rockwellautomation.com. We connect the imaginations of people with the potential of technology to expand what is humanly possible, making the world more productive and more sustainable. Headquartered in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, Rockwell Automation employs approximately 26,000 problem solvers dedicated to our customers in more than 100 countries. headline: Horsing around with the Vernon & District Drag Hounds
PostgreSQL 19's pg_plan_advice turned a 28ms query into 264ms under load
snippet: A ten-client pgbench run against a plain indexed lookup averaged 28ms a query. The same run, with one SET command telling PostgreSQL to use a sequential scan instead of the index it already wanted, averaged 264ms. Nothing else changed: same table, same data, same hardware, same query. That SET command is PostgreSQL 19's new pg_plan_advice, a contrib module that lets you hand the planner a hint string and watch it comply, or tell you exactly why it didn't. PostgreSQL 19 is still at RC2 as I write this, pulled from Docker Hub as postgres:19rc2 on 14 November. It isn't GA yet, so anything here could still shift before release. I went looking for a case where the hint would help. I didn't find one. What I found instead was a precise, well-documented way to make a healthy query slow, and a feedback system that is more honest about its own limits than most planner-hint tools I've used in other databases. The setup I built two tables: 50,000 customers and 2,000,000 orders, with status skewed so that 0.5% of orders are 'refunded' and the rest are 'shipped'. An index on status makes the refunded lookup cheap. This is the kind of table every production database has one of. CREATE INDEX idx_orders_status ON orders (status); ANALYZE; EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, COSTS OFF, TIMING OFF) SELECT c.region, count(*), sum(o.amount) FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.status = 'refunded' GROUP BY c.region; The planner picked an index scan on orders feeding a hash join against a sequential scan of the small customers table. Three repeated runs: 24.8ms (cold), 16.5ms, 18.0ms. That's the baseline for everything below. pg_plan_advice works in two halves. EXPLAIN (PLAN_ADVICE) tells you the advice string that would reproduce the plan you just got: Generated Plan Advice: JOIN_ORDER(o c) HASH_JOIN(c) SEQ_SCAN(c) INDEX_SCAN(o public.idx_orders_status) NO_GATHER(o c) And SET pg_plan_advice.advice = '...' feeds a string back in, which the planner then tries to honour, with feedback on how well it managed. Forcing the wrong plan I took the advice vocabulary (SEQ_SCAN, INDEX_SCAN, HASH_JOIN, NESTED_LOOP_PLAIN, and a dozen others for merge joins, partitionwise plans, and parallel workers) and used it to force the one plan the planner had already rejected: a sequential scan on orders instead of the index scan. Setup Single run Median of 3 Planner's own choice (index scan + hash join) 16.5 / 18.0 / 24.8 ms 18.0 ms Forced SEQ_SCAN(o), join left alone 46.1 / 51.7 / 43.6 ms 46.1 ms Forced SEQ_SCAN(o) + NESTED_LOOP_PLAIN(o c) 48.9 / 52.9 / 41.3 ms 48.9 ms Forcing just the scan method cost roughly as much as forcing the scan method and the join method together. The scan choice was doing almost all the work; the join strategy barely mattered once the input was a full table instead of 10,000 rows out of an index. Under concurrency the gap widened a lot further. I ran both plans through pgbench with 10 clients for 10 seconds: Plan Transactions Avg latency tps Planner's own choice 3,519 28.5 ms 351.3 Forced SEQ_SCAN(o) 384 264.0 ms 37.9 A 2.6x penalty on one connection became a 9.3x penalty on ten. Ten sequential scans over a 2-million-row table compete for the same buffer pages and CPU far harder than ten index probes do; the single-client number understates what a bad hint costs you in production. The opposite reading: I never found a case where it helped This is the part that mattered most to me. I expected to spend most of my time hunting for a query where PostgreSQL's planner gets it wrong and the hint fixes it. I built a schema where region and tier are perfectly correlated (both derived from the same id % 3), which should make the planner underestimate a combined filter on both columns under the independence assumption it still uses for most predicates. It did underestimate: a filter I knew matched 16,666 rows was costed as if it would match roughly a third of that. But the plan it picked anyway — a hash join — stayed the fastest option regardless, because the table was small enough that the misestimate never changed which plan was cheapest. I could not get PostgreSQL 19 RC2 to pick a genuinely bad default plan on this schema no matter how I skewed the correlation. Every advice string I supplied either matched what the planner already intended, or made things worse. That matches what I'd read going in: this is advice for pinning a plan you already trust, under a connection pooler or a parameter that occasionally throws the planner off, not a tool for correcting bad row estimates on the fly. I just hadn't believed it until I'd tried to break it for an hour and failed. What it refuses Three cases, with the exact feedback PostgreSQL gives: A nonexistent index: Supplied Plan Advice: INDEX_SCAN(o no_such_index) /* matched, inapplicable, failed */ Contradictory advice on the same table: SEQ_SCAN(o) /* matched, conflicting, failed */ INDEX_SCAN(o idx_orders_status) /* matched, conflicting, failed */ Both of these are refused safely — the query ran on the planner's own chosen plan, not a broken one. The one that worried me was a misspelled or missing table alias: SEQ_SCAN(zzz) /* not matched */ No error. No warning. The query just ran as if you'd supplied no advice at all, which is exactly what you'd want if you're testing, and exactly what you don't want if you've just typo'd an alias in a connection pooler's startup script and are now silently not getting the plan you think you configured. There is a documented fix: pg_plan_advice.feedback_warnings. With it on, the same typo produces a real log line: WARNING: supplied plan advice was not enforced DETAIL: advice SEQ_SCAN(zzz) feedback is "not matched" I turned it on and it did exactly what the documentation says. It's off by default, which means the failure mode most likely to bite someone — advice silently doing nothing — is also the one you have to opt into being told about. The documented caveat, and one it doesn't mention The docs warn that a cached prepared-statement plan won't notice a new pg_plan_advice.advice value until you run DISCARD PLANS. I reproduced this exactly. I forced plan_cache_mode = force_generic_plan so the first EXECUTE would cache a plan, set the advice to request a sequential scan, executed once (got the seq scan, as asked), then changed the advice to request the index scan and executed again: -- exec 2, advice changed to INDEX_SCAN, plan still cached from before Finalize Aggregate -> Gather -> Partial Aggregate -> Parallel Seq Scan on orders Still the seq scan. Only after DISCARD PLANS did the next execution switch to the index scan. What the docs don't mention: EXPLAIN (PLAN_ADVICE) against that stale cached execution showed no Supplied Plan Advice section at all, because no replanning happened. If you're checking whether your new advice took effect by looking for that section, its absence looks identical to "nothing was supplied," not "your advice was ignored." I'd have assumed I'd made a typo before I'd have suspected caching. What it costs when idle With the module loaded fresh via LOAD on every transaction, a trivial single-row count ran at 0.457ms average latency against 0.408ms with the module absent entirely — a real but small 12% tax, and it's the tax of calling LOAD every time, not the module's planning hook. Preloaded once via shared_preload_libraries, the same query ran at 0.377ms, indistinguishable from not having the module at all. If you're going to use this in production, preload it; don't LOAD it per connection. What I got wrong on the way I spent close to half my testing time chasing a theory that turned out false: that a prepared statement with a parameter on the skewed status column would flip to a bad generic plan after Postgres's usual five-execution custom-plan threshold, because I assumed the generic plan would use a naive uniform-selectivity estimate for an unbound parameter. It didn't. PostgreSQL's planner already uses the column's most-common-value statistics when building the generic plan, so it picked the index scan on execution six exactly as it had on execution one — 9.99ms down to 3.3ms, with no flip at all. The "advice fixes a plan regression" post I'd half-planned to write wasn't there. The honest finding was that the planner didn't need fixing, and the correlated-columns schema in the section above was my second attempt at the same thing, which also failed to produce a bad default plan. Run it yourself This needs Docker and about ten minutes. docker run -d --name pg19 -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=test postgres:19rc2 sleep 6 cat > runit.sql <<'SQL' CREATE TABLE customers (id bigint PRIMARY KEY, region text, tier text); CREATE TABLE orders (id bigint PRIMARY KEY, customer_id bigint REFERENCES customers(id), status text NOT NULL, amount numeric NOT NULL); INSERT INTO customers SELECT g, (ARRAY['eu','us','apac'])[1+g%3], (ARRAY['gold','silver','bronze'])[1+g%3] FROM generate_series(1,50000) g; INSERT INTO orders SELECT g, 1+(g%50000), CASE WHEN g % 200 = 0 THEN 'refunded' ELSE 'shipped' END, (random()*500)::numeric(10,2) FROM generate_series(1,2000000) g; LOAD 'pg_plan_advice'; -- the planner's own choice SELECT c.region, count(*), sum(o.amount) FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.status = 'refunded' GROUP BY c.region; -- force a sequential scan instead SET pg_plan_advice.advice = 'SEQ_SCAN(o)'; EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, COSTS OFF, TIMING OFF, PLAN_ADVICE) SQL docker cp runit.sql pg19:/tmp/runit.sql docker exec pg19 psql -U postgres -f /tmp/runit.sql For the concurrency numbers, swap the last EXPLAIN block for a pgbench custom script with the same SET line in it and run pgbench -U postgres -n -c 10 -T 10 -f script.sql postgres against both the advised and un-advised versions. Run your own forced-scan test through pgbench with at least ten clients before you pin a plan anywhere permanent, such as a pooler's startup script or postgresql.conf. My single-connection number was 2.6x. My ten-client number was 9.3x. Production traffic looks like the second number, not the first, and I almost stopped testing before I found that out.

headline: Tru-Juice seek fifth straight win against Racing United
snippet: KINGSTON, Jamaica—Leaders Tru-Juice FC and third place Racing United will meet today in what is expected to be an exciting Legend Jamaica Premier League first round game at Ferdie Neita Park at 3:00pm. Three points separate two of the highest-scoring teams in the league whose top scorers combine for almost 25 goals and the expectations are for a high intensity game. Also today, fourth-placed Montego Bay United travels to the Edward Seaga Complex to face Tivoli Gardens; Arnett Gardens are away to last-placed Humble Lion at Effortville; Cavalier FC hosts Treasure Beach at Turner’s Oval; and Dunbeholden FC are at home to Chapelton Maroons. At Ferdie Neita Park, Tru-Juice are the inform team in the competition and will be going after a fifth straight win, coming off a win over defending champions Portmore United. As proficient as they have been scoring goals, Tru-Juice have been better at stopping goals, and have conceded just two goals in their five-game unbeaten run. Tyrone Mullings who will face the team he represented up to last season, leads the goal scoring race with eight goals so far and will spearhead the Tru-Juice attack along with Daniel Roberts, the pair having combined for 12 of the team’s 18 goals scored so far. Racing United have failed to win any of their last two games, being ambushed by Treasure Beach and were held 0-0 by Chapelton Maroons last week and will hope to rebound today. Montego Bay United have cooled after a fast start and are winless in their last four games, playing to 2-2 draws in three of them while leading on each occasion. Last weekend’s draw against Molynes United frustrated coach Javier Ainstein as they gave up two goals in the first 10 minutes, rallied to level the scores by half time, but failed to get the winner despite dominating the second half. Tivoli Gardens are also going through a poor run as well, winning just once in their last five games and have slipped to eighth place but only a point off the top six places. One positive for MBU is that top scorer Jourdaine Fletcher has scored in back to back games and has taken his tally to five so far. Both teams have been leaking at the back however and have been conceding goals. Meanwhile, Arnett Gardens are quietly moving up the ladder and are coming off a good win over Waterhouse FC after holding Mount Pleasant FA to a 1-1 draw. They are expected to get the better of Humble Lion who are at the foot of the table. Humble Lion have conceded 12 goals in four straight losses and Arnett Gardens’ Giovanni Taylor who has scored seven goals so far, will be eager to face them. Cavalier FC completed a 3-0 win over Humble Lion on Thursday, scoring twice in the remaining 15 minutes of the game that was called off on Sunday due to heavy rain. They will face a Treasure Beach team that have been inconsistent, beating Racing United, losing to Portmore, then giving up a last minute goal to draw against Dunbeholden. Cavalier are off to yet another slow start this season, as they did last term and will be looking for a run of wins to get back into the top six. A win for Dunbeholden will take them past Chapelton Maroons in the points table, on goal-difference. Chapelton will need to find a replacement for goalkeeper Prince Daniel Smith who was sent off in time added in their 0-0 draw against Racing United on Monday.
